method.sim: Copy roguelike/tools/dev/sim/cb to a folder outside the datapack. rv_lib.py beside test_cb.py reuses its harness without running the sections: `src=open('test_cb.py').read(); g={'__name__':'rv','__file__':'test_cb.py'}; sys.argv=['test_cb.py',DP,'__none__']; exec(compile(src[:src.index('SECTIONS = [')],'test_cb.py','exec'),g); globals().update(g)` (gives world(), brain(), P(), G(), nopress(), full(), cm_hit(), pctx, Ctx, Ent, s.watch / s.calls). One game tick of rlk:tick lines 15-18 = tick_top(s,f,rc): s.gt+=1; #now cb=s.gt; hotbar.0 = a rlk_ui role:attack item; if f: the same item in weapon.offhand (sneakT 0); if rc: an interaction tagged atkBlock with data['interaction']; call rlk:player/def/input as the player; drop the offhand item; #dgOpen cb = (#now <= #dgEnd); remove rlk_dgo when #now == #dgKill.
method.real_server: A copy of the dev server dir <scratchpad>/mcsrv (jar <scratchpad>/mcjar/server.jar, JDK 25), started while holding the shared loadcheck lock (flock <scratchpad>/mcsrv/.lock), with this head as world/datapacks/roguelike and a small probe pack (namespace rvp) whose functions are quoted in each finding; commands go in through the console FIFO as tools/dev/loadcheck.sh does; results are read with `scoreboard players get` / `data get`. No client: an armor stand stands in for the player where a function only uses @s scores and items (`@a[tag=player]` parts do nothing).

findings.title: F mashing with gaps of 4 ticks or more is accepted every 12-15 ticks: the lock only stops perfectly regular mashing at 6.7 Hz or faster, so blind mashing parries most hits
findings.what: decisions.md: '패링 뒤 짧은 재사용 대기(헛누름 연타 방지)'; README 3 (line 804): '연타 금지'. An ignored press only moves parLk to max(parLk, now + #parRe 4) and f_key accepts when `now < parLk` is false. With presses every 4 t: +4 and +8 are ignored (the lock stays at +12), +12 is accepted. So any mash that contains gaps of 4 t or more re-arms as soon as the 12 t lock ends, and the lock is only 2 t longer than the tier window (#parW1 10): a whiffed press costs 2 ticks. After any parry (tier 1-3) par_use shortens the lock to hit tick + 2, so the next mash press opens a new window at once. A player who mashes F with no timing keeps 61-83 % of all ticks inside a tier window, takes 37-51 % of the unparried damage of every parriable attack (bosses too) and gets a perfect parry (damage 0, skill cooldown -1 s, one balance pip off the attacker) on 17-27 % of the hits. The only cost is that every accepted press cancels the normal attack in progress (player/def/press:5-10). The suite checks one cadence (3 t) and names it 'mashing ... is never accepted again'.
findings.evidence: (1) psim, the real path player/def/input -> f_key -> press / press_re, 1200 ticks, accepted presses and the share of ticks where a parriable strike would get tier 3 / 2 / 1 / none: period 1-3 t: 1 accepted, 99 % none; 4 t: 100 accepted, 25.0 / 25.0 / 33.3 / 16.7 %; 5 t: 80, 20 / 20 / 26.7 / 33.3; 6 t: 100, 25 / 25 / 33.3 / 16.7; 8 t: 75; 12 t: 100. Irregular gaps over 2400 t: gaps 3-4 t: 147 accepted, 61 % of ticks inside a window; 3-5 t: 162, 67 %; 4-6 t: 164, 68 %; 5-8 t: 169, 70 %; gaps 2-3 t: 1 accepted. (2) Same loop with real strikes (cm/hit_me through take_damage, 226 strikes at random 20-60 t gaps, 9000 t): no F = 36.0 HP per strike; F every 4 t = 13.3 (37 %), tiers none/1/2/3 = 38/67/62/59; every 5 t = 17.8 (49 %); every 6 t = 13.2 (37 %); 4 +-1 t = 18.4 (51 %); every 3 t = 36.0 (100 %). (3) Real 26.3 server, armor-stand stand-in, 240 ticks, presses every 1/2/3/4/5/6/8/12 t: accepted 1/1/1/20/16/20/15/20. (4) Arithmetic: press at 0 -> parLk 12; ignored at 4 -> max(12, 8) = 12; at 8 -> max(12, 12) = 12; at 12 -> 12 < 12 is false -> accepted.
findings.repro: sim: `for t in range(1200): s.gt += 1; s.setsc('#now','cb',s.gt); before = P(s,'parAt'); (put the UI item in weapon.offhand when t % period == 0); s.call('rlk:player/def/input', pctx(s)); inv.pop('weapon.offhand', None); acc += P(s,'parAt') != before`. Real server probe (per stand, each tick): `execute store result score #now cb run time query gametime` / `execute if score #r rvp matches 0 run item replace entity @s weapon.offhand with minecraft:stick[minecraft:custom_data={rlk_ui:{role:"attack"}}]` / `scoreboard players operation @s rvpLast = @s parAt` / `function rlk:player/def/input` / `item replace entity @s weapon.offhand with minecraft:air` / `execute unless score @s rvpLast = @s parAt run scoreboard players add @s rvpAcc 1`.
findings.fix: Make an ignored press push the lock a full lock length (now + #parGap, i.e. #parRe >= #parGap) so only a real pause re-arms; make a press whose window ran out unused cost clearly more than the window (for example lock = parAt + #parW1 + 8..10); decide whether a tier-1 parry should still shorten the lock to +2. Extend test_cb 'input' to periods 3..15 and irregular gaps, with an upper bound on accepted presses per second.

findings.title: A held right-click through the F5 use-item path now fires rclick_do every tick (rcT is reset in the same tick): fail-sound spam after every dodge, 스커크's fast move ends one tick after it starts
findings.what: In the F5 view (the only view now) a right-click that misses the eye shields is taken from the using_item advancement (rcU, README 13 '우클릭: 탄 채로 인터랙션 우클릭이 안 들어오는 경우를 대비해 ... 4틱마다'). The release tree (view/ride_tick) ran `rc_hold` if rcU, then `unless rcU -> rcT 0`, then `rcU 0`, so rcT counted the hold and rclick_do ran on ticks 1, 5, 9 ... The pre-pass calls player/def/rc first, which already sets rcU 0 (rc:5), and only then tests `if rcT 1.. unless rcU 1.. -> rcT 0` (input:10): rcT is 1 and rcU is 0, so rcT is reset every tick and `rcT % 4 == 1` holds on every held tick. Effects on any click that lasts 2 ticks or more on this path (a normal click is 2-3 ticks): (a) weapon slot: player/dash every tick, and dash_fail's new guard `if rcT matches 2.. return` never matches, so the denial sound snd/f228 plays on every tick of the cooldown, right after each dodge; (b) 스커크's skill slot: tick 1 dash_start, tick 2 `if skDash 1.. -> dash_end` (the 3 s fast move is over and the skill is on cooldown); (c) other skill / burst slots: char/deny (sound + actionbar) every tick instead of every 4th; (d) a held click dodges on the exact tick the cooldown ends. The map screen path (view/map_tick:10-12) keeps the old order and is not affected. Side note: on the interaction path (a held click on the eye shield repeats every 4 t in vanilla) rcT is not maintained either, so the fail sound still plays at +4 and +8 after each dodge although dash_fail's comment says held repeats are silent.
findings.evidence: (1) psim, rcU set to 1 before every tick (the advancement of the previous tick), weapon in hand, 30 ticks: rclick_do 30 calls (release tree: 8), dodges on ticks 0 / 12 / 24, dash_fail and snd/f228 on the other 27 ticks, rcT after the pre-pass = 0 on every tick. Skill item, #charN 3, held 3 ticks: tick 0 cast_skill -> dash_start (skDash 60); tick 1 cast_skill -> dash_end (skDash 0, skillCd 160). #charN 1 held 6 ticks: char/deny '원소전투 스킬 재사용 대기 중' on 5 of 6 ticks. (2) Real 26.3 server, armor-stand stand-in holding the weapon, rcU 1 every tick for 40 ticks: highest rcT seen after the pre-pass 0, the fail-sound flag #k198 snd set on 36 of 40 ticks, 4 dodges. (3) `git show 2dcc742:roguelike/data/rlk/function/view/ride_tick.mcfunction` (last lines) for the old order.
findings.repro: sim: `P(s,'rcU',1); s.call('rlk:player/def/input', pctx(s))` per tick with s.watch on rlk:combat/rclick_do, rlk:player/dash_go, rlk:player/dash_fail, rlk:snd/f228 (clear the snd scores each tick, decrement dashCool as player/tick:62). Real server, per tick as the stand (tags rvpH rlk_body, weapon.mainhand = stick with rlk_ui role attack): `scoreboard players reset #k198 snd` / `scoreboard players set @s rcU 1` / `function rlk:player/def/input` / `execute if score @s rcT > #H_rcTmax rvp run scoreboard players operation #H_rcTmax rvp = @s rcT` / `execute if score #k198 snd matches 1 run scoreboard players add #H_fail rvp 1` / `execute if score @s dashCool matches 1.. run scoreboard players remove @s dashCool 1`.
findings.fix: In player/def/input put the reset before the call (`execute if score @s rcT matches 1.. unless score @s rcU matches 1.. run scoreboard players set @s rcT 0`, then `execute if score @s rcU matches 1.. run function rlk:player/def/rc`), or let rc leave rcU for the caller to clear after the test. Add a dynamic check to test_cb (hold 30 ticks: rclick_do on ticks 1, 5, 9 ...; no fail sound while held).

findings.title: The perfect dodge's red afterimage is a mannequin removed with `kill`: in the game it plays the 20-tick vanilla death animation (pose DYING) and the death puff after its 8 ticks
findings.what: pd_ghost summons a living entity (minecraft:mannequin, invisible + Glowing, team rlk_cbred = the red outline) and player/def/fx/tick removes it with `kill @s` when cb reaches 0 (pd_ghost:2 kills an earlier one the same way). /kill on a living entity is lethal damage, not removal: the mannequin stops matching @e, stays 20 more ticks with DeathTime counting 1..19 in pose DYING (the outline tips over as a dying mob does) and is then removed with the death smoke puff. So the '8-tick' afterimage (README 3, user request 9: '퍼펙트 닷지는 빨간색 이펙트와 함께 피하는거라') is shown for 28 ticks, 20 of them as a falling red outline that ends in white smoke at the dodge start. Invulnerable:1b does not prevent it (the kill damage bypasses it). The simulator's kill removes at once, so 'fx: every effect entity is gone after 12 ticks' passes. The same holds for the mannequins the pack already killed before this lane (avatar, rlk_lure); only the ghost is new and is shown on every perfect dodge.
findings.evidence: Real 26.3 server. (1) A mannequin summoned with the ghost's NBT and a fixed UUID, `kill <uuid>` on probe tick 3, recorded every tick: `execute if entity @e[tag=rvpA]` = 1, 1, 0 from tick 3 on; `execute if entity <uuid>` = 1 up to tick 22 and 0 from tick 23; `data get entity <uuid> DeathTime` = 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 3, ... 19 (ticks 4-22). While it is dying every NBT read logs 'Failed to encode value 'DYING' to field 'pose': Invalid pose: dying'. (2) The pack's own ghost: `execute positioned 8.5 120 0.5 run function rlk:player/def/fx/pd_ghost`, aged by rlk:tick: @e[tag=rlk_cb_ghost] is 1 on ticks 1-6 and 0 at tick 8; about 0.7 s after the summon `data get entity <its uuid> DeathTime` = 12s; gone 0.5 s later. (3) Macro branch checked on the same server: profile = {texture:"rlk:skin/navia",model:"slim"}, team rlk_cbred has it as a member.
findings.repro: Real server: `summon minecraft:mannequin 0.5 120 0.5 {UUID:[I;1,2,3,4],Tags:["rvpA"],hide_description:1b,immovable:1b,NoGravity:1b,Invulnerable:1b,Silent:1b,Glowing:1b,active_effects:[{id:"minecraft:invisibility",duration:-1,amplifier:0,show_particles:0b,ambient:1b}]}`, three ticks later `kill 00000001-0000-0002-0000-000300000004`, then each tick `data get entity 00000001-0000-0002-0000-000300000004 DeathTime` and `execute if entity @e[tag=rvpA]`. In the game: any perfect dodge, watch the dodge start for 1.5 s.
findings.fix: Do not let the client see the death: one tick before the end switch the outline off and move it out of sight (`data merge entity @s {Glowing:0b}` and a tp far away), kill it on the next tick; or build the afterimage from a display entity (no death sequence). Check it in the game (README 0-9 already lists the ghost under '게임에서 확인할 것').

findings.title: Volley groups: a perfect parry leaves the group armed while a tier-1 / tier-2 parry disarms it, so the perfect parry is the worst parry outcome on a staggered volley
findings.what: hz/hurt and pj/hit mark the volley group (`grp_mark`: every other member harmless) only when `#dodged` is 0. Tier 3 sets #dodged 1, tiers 1-2 leave it 0. For a group whose members strike on different ticks, the press is spent after the first member (one press = one tick), so: perfect parry = first member 0 + the next member at full damage (unless the player presses again exactly then); tier 2 = 20 % once and the rest of the volley passes through; no parry = one full hit. README 3 states the rule as a lane decision; its consequence is that better timing gives a worse result. about 145 module files call mboss/grp_new (야타용왕 65, 아를레키노 27, 역장 21, 아펩 13, 나비 12, 타키 5, 홍련 2). Design decision for the lead; listed because the order of outcomes inverts.
findings.evidence: psim, two parriable disc hazards of one group (mbHzG 7) on a standing player, boss context, the first strikes at T, the second at T + 3, real F path: no parry: 54 HP + disarmed = 54; F 1 t before the first (tier 3): 0 + 54 = 54; F 4 t before (tier 2): 10 + disarmed = 10; F 8 t before (tier 1): 27 + disarmed = 27.
findings.repro: sim: two markers tagged rlk_mb_hz with mbHzK 1, mbHzD 100, mbHzG 7, mbHzND/NP/RA/Pm 0, mbHzHit 0 and a husk rlk_mb_body (#mbSt 1, #mbAtk 60, #mbDmgMul 100); per tick tick_top(s, f=...); at T and T + 3 `if mbHzHit == 0: s.call('rlk:mboss/hz/hurt', Ctx(hz, pos, (0,0)))`.
findings.fix: Either let a perfect parry consume the volley too (call grp_mark when #parT is 3), or let no parry tier consume it (mark only on #parT 0); then the three tiers are ordered again. Update README 3 and the suites that pin the rule (test_fw_az).

findings.title: The effect ager runs in the tick the effects are made: the perfect parry's screen jolt is rotated back in the same tick and the star's 2-tick growth is applied at spawn
findings.what: Every hit (view/tick, cm, Raiden, mboss) happens before rlk:tick line 85 (player/def/fx/world), so the first ageing pass is in the spawn tick. The jolt marker starts at cb 2: `rotate @s ~1.5 ~-1` in p3 and, the same tick, cb 2 -> 1 -> `rotate @s ~-1.5 ~1`: both rotation packets leave in one tick and the '화면이 1틱 짧게 튐' of README 3 never shows (with the pitch already at -90 the first step clamps and the second leaves a 1 degree drift). The star starts at cb 5 and t_star's `cb matches 4` branch (interpolation 2 t, scale x 1.5) runs before the entity was ever sent to the client, so it appears at 1.5 x with no growth and is visible 4 ticks, not 5. The warning glint (cb 6, change at cb 4) is not affected.
findings.evidence: psim: perfect parry on tick N then fx/world as rlk:tick does: N: `rotate @s ~1.5 ~-1`, `data merge entity @s {start_interpolation:0,interpolation_duration:2}`, `rotate @s ~-1.5 ~1`; N+2: the star's shrink; star cb 5 -> 4 and jolt cb 2 -> 1 inside tick N. Real 26.3 server, one function: fx/p3 then fx/world: star transformation.scale [1.25,1.25,1.25] -> [1.875,1.875,1.25] with interpolation_duration 2 in the same tick, jolt cb 1; two more passes: star scale [0,0,0], jolt gone.
findings.repro: sim: nopress(s); press(s, 1); cm_hit(s, e, 20); then `s.call('rlk:player/def/fx/world', C0)` once per tick, logging the rotate / data merge commands and the cb scores.
findings.fix: Start the counters one higher (jolt 3, star 6), or skip entities tagged rlk_cb_new in the first pass and drop that tag at the end of fx/world.

findings.title: The red afterimage faces south (yaw 0) whenever the perfect dodge is found through the dodge-start box, which is every perfect dodge against custom mobs
findings.what: pd_at takes the ghost's facing from `rotated as @e[tag=rlk_body,limit=1]`. During cm/world and cm/pj/world of the window, in mboss/near_all and in Raiden's try_near the rlk_body tag sits on the rlk_dgo interaction, which dodge_stamp summons without a rotation (yaw 0). The afterimage is meant to be the character as it stood ('아바타가 보던 쪽', pd_ghost:1). Only a perfect dodge judged at the real body (a boss hazard that still covers the moved body) faces correctly.
findings.evidence: Real 26.3 server: stand-in body with Rotation [135f,0f]; dodge_stamp at it; ghost_on -> player/def/fx/pd -> ghost_off: the ghost's Rotation = [0.0f,0.0f] (position = the dodge start, correct); the same fx/pd without ghost_on: Rotation [135.0f,0.0f]. rlk_dgo Rotation [0.0f,0.0f].
findings.repro: Real server function: summon an armor stand {Tags:["rvpR","rlk_body"],Rotation:[135f,0f]}; `execute as @e[tag=rvpR] at @s run function rlk:player/def/dodge_stamp`; `function rlk:player/def/ghost_on`; `execute as @e[tag=rvpR] run function rlk:player/def/fx/pd`; `function rlk:player/def/ghost_off`; `data get entity @e[tag=rlk_cb_ghost,limit=1] Rotation`.
findings.fix: Give the box the body's yaw in dodge_stamp (`execute rotated as <body> run tp @e[tag=rlk_dgo] ~ ~ ~ ~ 0` after the summon), or use rlk_body_real when it exists in pd_at.

findings.title: A player saved before the overhaul loses the first perfect dodge: the judge's lazy reset wipes the dodge stamp it is about to read, and the dodge-start box is left behind
findings.what: rlk:load resets the five stamps only for players online when it runs (none at a server or world start), and player/tick never does (init is already 1). dodge_stamp writes dgAt, #dgEnd, #dgKill without creating parHit. The first judged hit then runs `unless score @s parHit ... run reset`, which sets dgAt and dgRw to -1000000 and the globals #dgEnd / #dgKill too: the dodge of that tick is gone (full hit, no reward) and rlk:tick never reaches #now = #dgKill, so the rlk_dgo interaction stays until the next dodge. Once per player per world, only when the first judged event is a hit inside a dodge window (an F press or any earlier hit initialises the stamps). The box is also left behind when rlk:tick returns before line 18 on the kill tick (two tagged players) or its chunk is not loaded on that tick (a teleport, a server stop inside the 3 ticks); the next dodge removes it, nothing reads it meanwhile.
findings.evidence: psim, the five stamps removed from the player, the real right-click path, a swordsman's strike in the same tick: HP lost 36, #dodged 0, #pdg 0, dgAt -1000000, #dgKill -1000000, one rlk_dgo left after 6 more ticks (initialised player: 0 lost, #pdg 1, +1000 energy, box gone). Real 26.3 server, a new armor stand: dodge_stamp -> dgAt 34217 (= gametime); judge with #hcC 0 in the same tick -> #dodged 0, dgAt -1000000, #dgKill cb -1000000; rlk_dgo still there 6 ticks later.
findings.repro: sim: `for o in ('parAt','parLk','parHit','dgAt','dgRw'): s.scores.pop((('e', pl.id), o), None)`; tick_top(s, rc=True); strike through cm/hit_me. Real server as a new armor stand: `function rlk:player/def/dodge_stamp`, set #hcC/#hcK/#hcNP/#hcND/#dodged tmp, `function rlk:player/def/judge`.
findings.fix: Run the `unless score @s parHit ...` reset at the top of player/def/input (before F and the right-click) or in player/tick, or make reset fill only the missing stamps and leave #dgEnd / #dgKill alone. A periodic `kill @e[tag=rlk_dgo]` when #dgOpen is 0 would also clear a stranded box.

findings.title: F and a right-click that arrive in the same tick: the click is consumed but no dodge starts (the weapon is in the off hand when rclick_do tests the main hand)
findings.what: The F swap puts the slot-0 weapon in the off hand until player/hotbar/tick restores it later in the tick. The pre-pass handles F (line 4) and then the interaction right-click (line 7): poll_right removes the interaction data and calls rclick_do, whose three `if items entity @s weapon.mainhand ...` tests all fail on the empty hand. Parry stamp yes, dodge no, no cooldown. The harness cannot show it: psim resolves weapon.mainhand to hotbar.0 and the F tests put the item in the off hand without emptying the hand.
findings.evidence: psim with hotbar.0 emptied as the swap does, the UI item in weapon.offhand and an atkBlock interaction with data: after player/def/input parAt == now, dgAt unchanged, the interaction data gone, dashCool 0.
findings.repro: sim: inv['weapon.offhand'] = UI; inv.pop('hotbar.0', None); atkBlock.data['interaction'] = {...}; s.call('rlk:player/def/input', pctx(s)).
findings.fix: In the pre-pass, when the off hand holds the rlk_ui role:attack item, treat the right-click as the weapon's (call player/dash directly), or handle the right-click before F.

findings.title: The F5 crosshair is not sent again when a parry / dodge overlay ends: it stays off up to 9 ticks longer (tier 3: 6-15 t, tier 2: 4-13 t, perfect dodge: 10-19 t)
findings.what: The overlays use the title line that carries the F5 crosshair glyph and set vBig = in + hold + out. ride_tick sends the crosshair only when its 10-tick counter #xh is 0 and vBig is 0, and nothing re-sends it when vBig runs out. After every tier-2 / tier-3 parry and every perfect dodge the aim point is missing for the overlay plus 0-9 ticks (mean 4.5). The same pattern existed for rare overlays (boss kits, 화무십일홍's vignette); the parry / dodge overlays make it a constant of combat. From the code path only (the simulator has no client).
findings.evidence: g/title: `title ... times in hold out`, the glyph, `vBig = t`; view/tick:7 lowers vBig once per tick; ride_tick:16-18: `#xh += 1; if #xh >= 10 -> 0; if #xh == 0 unless vBig >= 1 -> view/xhair` (times 0 25 0 + the glyph).
findings.repro: In the game: perfect-dodge or perfect-parry and watch the centre dot; or log view/xhair calls around an overlay.
findings.fix: When vBig reaches 0 force the next send (set #xh view to 9 in view/tick's vBig line when it goes 1 -> 0), or add the crosshair glyph to the overlay components.

findings.title: README / comments that no longer match: the 'press tick = 0 on every path' claim, effect timings, boss sections that still describe dash i-frames, stale headers
findings.what: (a) README 2 '어느 경로로 눌러도 누른 틱 = 0 이 같다': not for the F5 use-item path. using_item fires in the player's own tick, after that tick's functions, so a click seen by tick N stamps dgAt = N + 1; F and a click on the eye shield stamp N. One tick of a 3-tick window. (b) README 3 효과: the jolt '1틱', the star '2틱 커졌다', the ghost '8틱' (A-05, A-03). (c) Boss sections still say 대시 / 대시 무적 for current behaviour: 타키 nova '대시로 피함' (2052; now a perfect dodge or i-frames only), 아를레키노 '둘 다 생명의 계약, 대시로 피함' (2192, 2201), 나루카미 '달리기·대시로' (2905), 나비아 '대쉬가 잠기고' (2778), 홍련 2247-2339 (the dash i-frame pip rule, '대시 경제' with 2 charges, T6 / T7; contradicts README 3 line 839; lane H rewrites that section), and '샘플 대비 달라진 점' 2662 '대쉬 = 충전식, F / Shift+F 동작 없음'. (d) reset.mcfunction's header says it runs at run start, death and revive; its only callers are player/init, load, f_key and judge (harmless: the stamps are game times). (e) dash_fail's comment about silent held repeats (A-02). (f) the generated boss/azhdaha/brand/dodge.mcfunction:1 still documents the old #mbDodgeOk rule (tell >= 12 t).
findings.evidence: grep -n '대시\|대쉬' roguelike/README.md; grep -rn 'player/def/reset' roguelike/data; vanilla: ServerPlayer.updateUsingItem triggers using_item from the player tick.
findings.repro: Read the lines; for (a) compare input.mcfunction:7 (interaction data, same tick) with :9 (rcU, set by the advancement one tick earlier).
findings.fix: Correct the lines; for (a) either say so or stamp the rcU path's dodge one tick back.

findings.title: Test gaps that let the above through: one mash cadence, static-only checks for the held click and Raiden's re-test, boss simulators that never run the pre-pass or the near pass
findings.what: (1) 'input: mashing F every 3 t (or a held key repeating) is never accepted again' tests the one cadence the lock stops (A-01). (2) The held right-click has only a string check ('view/ride_tick no longer handles rcU'); nothing runs rcU through the pre-pass for more than one tick (A-02). (3) Raiden's try_near is checked by the presence of the string 'hazard/try_near'; pj/near is not run at all; hz/near is run directly on a hand-built hazard. The boss world loops (azsim.world, fgsim.world, hrsim.world_sc; no file under hr/tests/lib, az/tests_cm/lib, ar/tests/lib, ar/s3/lib names them) call mboss/main only: no player/def/input, no cm ghost swap, no mboss/near_all, so no fight suite or m0diff run exercises or counts them (I ran pj/near through near_all and Raiden's try in psim: both behave as designed). findings.title: Balance note (overlaps reviewer B): dodging on cooldown with no timing avoids about half of normal / elite strikes while standing still and pays energy
findings.what: The dodge has no whiff cost: 7 of every 12 ticks (9 with 질주 2: 12 x 80 / 100 = 9.6 -> 9, i.e. -25 %, lore says -20 %) avoid a normal or elite strike and 3 of them are a perfect dodge with +10 energy, against bosses too. The old dash gave 6 i-frame ticks per 20 t charge and no energy. Together with A-01 a player can hold both inputs and ignore timing against ordinary rooms. For the lead / B to weigh; the windows themselves are as decided.
